brief: Tree (n<=2e5), all white. Paint a start vertex, then repeatedly paint a white vertex adjacent to a black one, scoring the size of its white component each time. Maximise total score.
key_idea: Once the start is fixed the score is always the sum of subtree sizes when rooted there; reroot: f(child) = f(parent) - sz[child] + (n - sz[child]).
solution:
1. Root at 1, compute subtree sizes (iterative BFS order).
2. f(1) = sum of sz.
3. For each child v of p: f(v) = f(p) - sz[v] + n - sz[v].
4. Answer max f.

brief: Array a (n<=2e5). Maximise the median (lower median) over subarrays of length >= k.
key_idea: Median >= x iff some window of length >= k has more elements >= x than < x: map to +1/-1 and test with prefix sums + running prefix minimum.
solution:
1. Binary search x in [1,n].
2. b_i = +1 if a_i >= x else -1; prefix sums P.
3. For r >= k: mn = min(mn, P[r-k]); if P[r] - mn > 0 -> feasible.
4. Largest feasible x is the answer.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: Tree with n<=1e5 rooms; m queries (x,y): count rooms equidistant from x and y.
key_idea: Binary lifting LCA; if dist is even, the equidistant rooms are those hanging off the midpoint except the branches toward x and y.
solution:
1. Root at 1: depth, subtree sizes, binary lifting table.
2. x==y -> n. d = dist(x,y) odd -> 0.
3. Let x be deeper. If depth[x]==depth[y]: midpoint = lca; answer n - sz[child toward x] - sz[child toward y].
4. Else mid = ancestor of x at d/2 up; answer sz[mid] - sz[ancestor of x at d/2-1].
5. Brute-force checked on random small trees.
complexity: O((n+m) log n) time, O(n log n) space

brief: Choose exactly k of n<=200 numbers (<=1e18) to maximise the trailing zeros of their product.
key_idea: Trailing zeros = min(#2, #5); knapsack dp[j][fives] = max twos using j numbers.
solution:
1. Count t (factors of 2) and f (factors of 5) per number (f <= 25).
2. dp[j][s] = max total twos with j chosen numbers and s total fives (-1 = impossible).
3. Iterate items, j downward: dp[j][s] = max(dp[j][s], dp[j-1][s-f] + t).
4. Answer = max over s of min(s, dp[k][s]).
complexity: O(n * k * 25n) ~ 2e8 simple ops, O(k * 25n) space

brief: Array (n<=500). Replace two adjacent equal elements v,v by one v+1, any number of times. Minimum final length.
key_idea: val[l][r] = the single value segment l..r can collapse to (or -1); then the minimum number of collapsible pieces covering the array.
solution:
1. val[i][i] = a_i.
2. val[l][r] = val[l][k]+1 if some split k has val[l][k] == val[k+1][r] != -1.
3. dp[i] = min over j<i with val[j][i-1] != -1 of dp[j] + 1.
4. Answer dp[n].

brief: Tree of n<=3e5 cities with k police stations; every city is within d of a station. Remove as many roads as possible keeping that true; print removed roads.
key_idea: Multi-source BFS from all stations: keep only BFS-tree edges; every other edge can be removed (each city keeps its shortest route to the nearest station).
solution:
1. Push all distinct station cities into the queue with dist 0.
2. BFS: when a new city is discovered through edge id, mark that edge as kept.
3. Remove every unmarked edge (count = #distinct stations - 1).
4. Distances never increase, so the law (<= d) still holds.

brief: n x m grid (<=20x20) of numbers. Count right/down paths from (1,1) to (n,m) whose XOR of all cells equals k.
key_idea: Meet in the middle on the anti-diagonal i+j = (n+m-2)/2: store XOR counts per middle cell from the start, then walk back from the end and look up x ^ k.
solution:
1. half = (n+m-2)/2.
2. DFS from (0,0) to cells with i+j == half, XOR including the middle cell; mp[i][x]++.
3. DFS backwards from (n-1,m-1) to the same diagonal, XOR excluding the middle cell; ans += mp[i][x ^ k].
4. Each half has at most 2^19 paths.
dry_run:
Sample 1 (3x3, k=11): half=2; forward XORs at diagonal cells, backward lookups.
Three paths match.
Answer 3.

brief: Count pairs of positive integers (a,b) with c*lcm(a,b) - d*gcd(a,b) = x (c,d,x <= 1e7, t <= 1e4 tests).
key_idea: Write a=g*p, b=g*q with gcd(p,q)=1: g*(c*p*q - d) = x, so g | x and p*q = (x/g + d)/c; a coprime ordered split of L into p*q has 2^omega(L) ways.
solution:
1. Sieve omega(L) (number of distinct primes) up to 2e7.
2. For each divisor g of x (trial division to sqrt x): s = x/g + d.
3. If c | s: ans += 2^omega(s/c).
4. Print ans.
complexity: O(V log log V) sieve + O(sqrt x) per test

brief: n trees (heights a increasing, a_1=1); each unit cut needs a recharge costing b_i where i is the largest index of a fully cut tree (b decreasing, b_n=0). Minimise total cost to cut all trees.
key_idea: Only the chain of trees cut 'to completion' matters: dp[i] = min_{j<i} dp[j] + b_j * a_i; slopes b_j decrease and queries a_i increase -> monotonic convex hull trick.
solution:
1. dp[0] = 0 (first tree has height 1, cut with the initial charge).
2. dp[i] = min over j<i of dp[j] + b_j*a_i.
3. Lines (slope b_j, intercept dp[j]) added in decreasing slope; queries increasing -> deque, pop front while the next line is better.
4. Use __int128 in the intersection test. Answer dp[n-1] (after tree n everything is free).

brief: n x m matrix (<=70). From each row pick at most floor(m/2) elements; maximise the total sum that is divisible by k.
key_idea: Per row knapsack r[count][sum mod k] (count <= m/2), reduce to best[rem]; then combine rows with a dp over remainders.
solution:
1. For each row: r[c][q] = max sum choosing c elements with sum % k == q (0/1 knapsack, c downward).
2. best[q] = max over c of r[c][q].
3. tot'[(a+q)%k] = max(tot[a] + best[q]).
4. Answer tot[0] (0 allowed).
complexity: O(n * m * (m/2) * k + n * k^2) time
dry_run:
Sample 1: row picks (2,4)=6, (5,2)=7, (7,4)=11.
Total 24, divisible by 3.
Answer 24.

brief: Forest of n<=3e5 cities; queries: report the longest path in x's component, or merge two components with one road chosen to minimise the new longest path.
key_idea: Store each component's diameter in a DSU; joining the centres gives new diameter max(d1, d2, ceil(d1/2) + ceil(d2/2) + 1).
solution:
1. Union initial edges; compute each tree's diameter with two BFS runs.
2. Query 1: print dia[find(x)].
3. Query 2 (different sets): dia = max(d1, d2, (d1+1)/2 + (d2+1)/2 + 1), union.
4. Path compression (iterative).

brief: Directed graph, d = BFS distance from city 1. From each start you may move along edges to larger d freely and at most once along an edge to d <= current. For each start, minimal reachable d.
key_idea: Process vertices by decreasing d: best[v] = min(d[v], d[u] for edges v->u with d[u] <= d[v] (use the special move now), best[u] for edges with d[u] > d[v] (move freely)).
solution:
1. BFS from 1 for d.
2. Visit vertices in reverse BFS order (non-increasing d).
3. best[v] = d[v]; for v->u: if d[u] > d[v] best[v] = min(best[v], best[u]); else best[v] = min(best[v], d[u]).
4. Print best[1..n].
